# Visual design execution rules
## Color
Define canvas, surface, text, muted, border, accent, positive, negative, warning, neutral and categorical/sequential/diverging scales. Use consistent semantic mappings and redundant labels/icons; color alone must not convey status. Aim for WCAG AA text contrast (4.5:1 normal, 3:1 large) and relevant non-text contrast. Example editorial palette: canvas #F5F3EE, surface #FFFFFF, text #202A28, muted #52615D, accent #285B4D, warning #946000, negative #A33C32. Alternative industrial dark: canvas #15201F, surface #22302E, text #F1F4F2, accent #9AC9B8. These are starting tokens, not audited palettes; test actual pairs. Do not assume cultural color meanings are universal.
## Typography
Choose a coherent sans or editorial serif/sans pairing, with CJK fallback and tabular numerals. Example desktop scale 12/14/16/22/32/48px, adjust for projection and density. Use line-height around 1.4–1.6 for prose, align numeric columns, show units, avoid tiny labels and all-caps Chinese headings. No unlicensed font redistribution.
## Layout
Select Matrix (monitoring/comparison), Editorial (claim/evidence), Hierarchical (overview/detail), Flow (sequence), Spatial (geographic/physical). Compose around one dominant task per scene. Use 4/8px spacing rhythm, aligned baselines, deliberate asymmetry, sufficient whitespace, direct chart annotations, adjacent evidence. Avoid equal cards by default; use tables for dense lookup. Responsive order must preserve meaning; test 390, 1440, 1920px widths.
## Material
Matte paper for editorial evidence; glass for contextual overlays with opaque fallback; parchment for historical/archive context; metal/instrument for industrial interfaces; terrain/solid volumes for spatial structure; wireframe for topology. Define role, opacity, texture, shadow and contrast per layer. Never obscure labels with blur, texture, specular effects or perspective. Material associations are design hypotheses, not universal psychology.
## Chart selection
Ranking: sorted bar/dot; target deviation: diverging bar/bullet; time: line/small multiples; composition: stacked bar/treemap; distribution: histogram/box/ECDF; relationship: scatter; contribution: waterfall only for additive quantities; flow: Sankey only with reconciled flows; geography: choropleth for normalized rates, proportional symbols for totals; precise lookup: table. For engineering, architecture, science and networks consult domain routing and catalog. Separate canonical type from projection, material and animation. Avoid 3D distortion of quantitative comparisons, misleading axes, fabricated uncertainty or causal claims.
## Diagrams and space
Model nodes, edges, ports, groups and direction before layout. Use orthogonal routing or ELK when appropriate, minimize crossings without altering topology, preserve labels and swimlane semantics. Maps need grounded geometry, projection, legend and scale when relevant; simplified geometry must be labeled. 3D requires a genuine spatial task or clear illustrative purpose, not decorative extrusion alone. Never imply engineering-standard accuracy without verification.
## Motion and interaction
Define trigger, state, affected IDs, transition, duration, easing, interrupt/reset, keyboard/touch fallback. Suggested durations 120–250ms micro, 250–500ms scene, longer only for explanatory sequence; not mandatory. Maintain object constancy, preserve filters and selection, provide static/reduced-motion alternative. Use progressive disclosure, linked highlighting, drilldown, scenario presets, source inspection; essential evidence visible without hover. Model inputs must have bounds, units and assumptions. Avoid perpetual decorative animation.
## Visual specification
Record chosen art direction, rejected alternatives, token values, typography scale, layout per scene, chart encoding and rejected alternative, material roles, interaction state map, responsive strategy, and dependencies. Reference actual repo examples when relevant rather than copying a generic dashboard.

# Color intelligence V1.2
Separate atmosphere from data semantics: categorical identity, ordered magnitude, signed deviation, status. Unknown differs from zero. Status needs text or shape. Choose hue and chroma by context, not universal emotional claims. Generate in OKLCH, reduce chroma to fit sRGB, measure contrast after quantization. Fixed lightness recipes and binary chroma reduction are not optimal gamut mapping. WCAG AA normal text 4.5:1, large text 3:1, relevant non-text UI 3:1 subject to exceptions. Audit composited backgrounds and states separately. Sequential scale is not certified CVD safe. Categorical/diverging and CVD simulation pending.
Reference starting points, not freshly retrieved: https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/ ; https://www.w3.org/TR/css-color-4/ ; https://bottosson.github.io/posts/oklab/ ; https://colorbrewer2.org/ ; doi:10.1038/s41467-020-19160-7.
Twelve candidate themes, 72 opaque text pairs checked. No browser or audience validation.

--- visual-intelligence/semantic-color.md ---
# Semantic color
Categorical: stable IDs, unordered hues, direct labels or shapes. Greedy maximin search across normal and three full-severity simulated vision modes; deterministic but not globally optimal. Background contrast filter 3:1 is a candidate graphic check, not text certification. Diverging: odd count, neutral midpoint, symmetric OKLCH lightness schedule; map to meaningful numeric center and explicit bounds, disclose asymmetric domains. Unknown separate from zero. Status: use text/icons and domain meaning, never infer good/bad from sign alone. CVD simulation uses Machado et al. 2009 full-severity matrices in linear sRGB, clips output; not a clinical model or guarantee. OKLab Euclidean distances are heuristics, no universal pass threshold. Reference: https://www.inf.ufrgs.br/~oliveira/pubs_files/CVD_Simulation/CVD_Simulation.html (not freshly retrieved).

--- visual-intelligence/color-art.md ---
# Color art direction
Harmony is a compositional hypothesis, not a universal beauty law. Six hue relationships: monochrome, analogous, complementary, split complementary, triadic, neutral plus accent. Use neutral/support/accent area guide 75/20/5 only as starting heuristic, not measured pixel coverage. Visual weight depends on area, local contrast, saturation, position and surrounding content. Reserve high contrast for focal claims. Warm/cool meanings vary by culture and context. Preserve supplied brand hex exactly; restrict role if contrast fails, do not silently recolor. Keep semantic data palettes independent. Overlay helper approximates encoded sRGB source-over on one opaque backdrop; actual browser compositing, blur, gradients and layered materials need inspection. Eight candidate directions are generated, not reverse-engineered or audience validated. References for later reading: Josef Albers Interaction of Color; Johannes Itten The Art of Color; CSS Compositing and Blending Level 1 https://www.w3.org/TR/compositing-1/. No fresh source review in this increment.

--- visual-intelligence/typography-foundations.md ---
# Typography foundations V1.2
Typography is information hierarchy, not font decoration. Establish semantic roles before styling: display, heading, subheading, body, label, note, metric. Use size, weight, spacing, alignment and position before adding color. Do not force every role onto every page.
Three initial directions: editorial (serif headings, sans body), Swiss-inspired (sans hierarchy, grid), technical (compact sans, aligned numbers). These are candidate recipes, not historical reproductions. Font stacks are fallbacks, not bundled fonts; actual availability and CJK glyph coverage vary.
Numbers: use tabular lining figures for comparable columns if supported; align values by consistent units/precision, show minus signs and missing values explicitly; do not round away material differences. Large display metrics can use proportional figures. Decimal alignment needs layout support, not merely tabular figures.
Chinese/mixed: preserve punctuation and language-specific line breaking, avoid blanket letter spacing, avoid forced breaks inside Latin words and units where feasible; use lang attributes for language runs. 36em Chinese and 65ch English are starting measure heuristics, not accessibility requirements. CSS overflow-wrap anywhere is emergency wrapping. Test long labels, zoom, font fallback and narrow screens.
Reference reading queue (not freshly retrieved): https://www.w3.org/TR/clreq/ ; https://www.w3.org/TR/css-text-3/ ; https://www.w3.org/TR/css-fonts-4/ ; https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/text-spacing.html ; Robert Bringhurst, The Elements of Typographic Style; Josef Müller-Brockmann, Grid Systems in Graphic Design.
The module generates candidate tokens and CSS. It does not measure glyphs, enforce actual line length, guarantee font features or certify accessibility.

--- visual-intelligence/composition-fundamentals.md ---
# Composition fundamentals
Eight candidate principles: proximity, similarity, figure-ground, continuity, closure, visual weight, balance, tension. Distinguish semantic relationships, geometric placement and perceptual response. Start with intended focal claim, supporting evidence, reading order and constraints; then generate alternative compositions. The audit computes bounding-box intersections, canvas overflow and area × declared emphasis centroid only. It cannot measure actual attention, typography, contrast, perceived balance or beauty. Intentional overlap requires review. Reference reading queue (not freshly retrieved): Wertheimer, Laws of Organization in Perceptual Forms; Rudolf Arnheim, Art and Visual Perception; Colin Ware, Information Visualization: Perception for Design; Wagemans et al., A Century of Gestalt Psychology in Visual Perception, 2012, doi:10.1037/a0029333. Seven inline logic checks passed; no browser or reader study.

--- visual-intelligence/material-foundations.md ---
# Material perception foundations
Distinguish physical material, perceptual cues and semantic associations. Ten cue categories; six normalized design descriptors with three illustrative profiles. Values are authored examples, not measured optical properties. Roughness changes highlight spread under fixed illumination; alpha is not optical transmission; metalness is a rendering workflow parameter; texture and relief are distinct. Semantic associations depend on audience and context. Keep essential text on stable readable surfaces. Reading queue (not freshly retrieved): Fleming, Visual perception of materials and their properties (2014), doi:10.1016/j.visres.2013.11.004; Pharr et al., Physically Based Rendering, https://pbr-book.org/4ed/; Khronos glTF 2.0 specification, https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html. Ten inline checks passed; no optical simulation, CSS renderer or reader study.

--- visual-intelligence/motion-foundations.md ---
# Motion perception foundations
Eight candidate semantic roles, not an exhaustive perceptual taxonomy. Preserve object identity, distinguish actual data change from camera movement, keep essential facts visible without animation. Evidence references required for causal, temporal and transformation claims; references are not verified. Reduced-motion plan sets effective duration to zero; runtime must implement it. Durations are authored, not empirically optimized. Reading queue: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/animation-from-interactions.html ; Heer and Robertson, Animated Transitions in Statistical Data Graphics (2007); Tversky et al., Animation: Can It Facilitate? (2002). References not freshly reviewed. Nine inline checks passed; no browser, perception or audience tests.

# Representation foundations
Six layers: information ontology, relational structure, cognitive task, visual encoding, representation, rendering. Sixteen candidate relation/task mappings; not exhaustive and not a replacement for the existing catalog. Position and length are preferred candidates for precise magnitude comparison; geographic position and physical geometry carry domain semantics. Missing fields block eligibility, but declarations do not establish truth, compatible units, geometry validity or causal identification. No renderer or catalog audit. 33 inline checks passed. # Visual design execution rules
## Color
Define canvas, surface, text, muted, border, accent, positive, negative, warning, neutral and categorical/sequential/diverging scales. Use consistent semantic mappings and redundant labels/icons; color alone must not convey status. Aim for WCAG AA text contrast (4.5:1 normal, 3:1 large) and relevant non-text contrast. Example editorial palette: canvas #F5F3EE, surface #FFFFFF, text #202A28, muted #52615D, accent #285B4D, warning #946000, negative #A33C32. Alternative industrial dark: canvas #15201F, surface #22302E, text #F1F4F2, accent #9AC9B8. These are starting tokens, not audited palettes; test actual pairs. Do not assume cultural color meanings are universal.
## Typography
Choose a coherent sans or editorial serif/sans pairing, with CJK fallback and tabular numerals. Example desktop scale 12/14/16/22/32/48px, adjust for projection and density. Use line-height around 1.4–1.6 for prose, align numeric columns, show units, avoid tiny labels and all-caps Chinese headings. No unlicensed font redistribution.
## Layout
Select Matrix (monitoring/comparison), Editorial (claim/evidence), Hierarchical (overview/detail), Flow (sequence), Spatial (geographic/physical). Compose around one dominant task per scene. Use 4/8px spacing rhythm, aligned baselines, deliberate asymmetry, sufficient whitespace, direct chart annotations, adjacent evidence. Avoid equal cards by default; use tables for dense lookup. Responsive order must preserve meaning; test 390, 1440, 1920px widths.
## Material
Matte paper for editorial evidence; glass for contextual overlays with opaque fallback; parchment for historical/archive context; metal/instrument for industrial interfaces; terrain/solid volumes for spatial structure; wireframe for topology. Define role, opacity, texture, shadow and contrast per layer. Never obscure labels with blur, texture, specular effects or perspective. Material associations are design hypotheses, not universal psychology.
## Chart selection
Ranking: sorted bar/dot; target deviation: diverging bar/bullet; time: line/small multiples; composition: stacked bar/treemap; distribution: histogram/box/ECDF; relationship: scatter; contribution: waterfall only for additive quantities; flow: Sankey only with reconciled flows; geography: choropleth for normalized rates, proportional symbols for totals; precise lookup: table. For engineering, architecture, science and networks consult domain routing and catalog. Separate canonical type from projection, material and animation. Avoid 3D distortion of quantitative comparisons, misleading axes, fabricated uncertainty or causal claims.
## Diagrams and space
Model nodes, edges, ports, groups and direction before layout. Use orthogonal routing or ELK when appropriate, minimize crossings without altering topology, preserve labels and swimlane semantics. Maps need grounded geometry, projection, legend and scale when relevant; simplified geometry must be labeled. 3D requires a genuine spatial task or clear illustrative purpose, not decorative extrusion alone. Never imply engineering-standard accuracy without verification.
## Motion and interaction
Define trigger, state, affected IDs, transition, duration, easing, interrupt/reset, keyboard/touch fallback. Suggested durations 120–250ms micro, 250–500ms scene, longer only for explanatory sequence; not mandatory. Maintain object constancy, preserve filters and selection, provide static/reduced-motion alternative. Use progressive disclosure, linked highlighting, drilldown, scenario presets, source inspection; essential evidence visible without hover. Model inputs must have bounds, units and assumptions. Avoid perpetual decorative animation.
## Visual specification
Record chosen art direction, rejected alternatives, token values, typography scale, layout per scene, chart encoding and rejected alternative, material roles, interaction state map, responsive strategy, and dependencies. Reference actual repo examples when relevant rather than copying a generic dashboard.

# Narrative Design V1.0
## Operating contract
Use for authored business narratives; for monitoring or exploratory dashboards, prioritize user tasks and do not manufacture a thesis. Never invent evidence, causal attribution, targets or user-test results. Distinguish observations, hypotheses, forecasts and decisions. Preserve contradictory evidence and source access.
## Workflow
1. G1 Evidence: inventory sources, grain, period, units, definitions, missingness and reconciliations. Stop on material unresolved errors; mark missing inputs.
2. G2 Thesis: generate three candidate questions or claims, compare relevance, support and actionability. Select one or retain an open question. Record rejected alternatives.
3. G3 Spine: choose a primary spine and archetype from references/atlas.md. Assign every chapter a role; remove redundant content without hiding material exceptions.
4. G4 Naked narrative: write a short executive summary and full prose argument. Link each material claim to evidence IDs; include counterevidence and uncertainty. Do not proceed if the argument fails.
5. G5 Storyboard: specify audience, time budget, cognitive before/after, chapter question, evidence, visual task, transition and interaction. Use templates/storyboard.json and schema. Essential information must be visible without interaction.

# Visual design execution rules
## Color
Define canvas, surface, text, muted, border, accent, positive, negative, warning, neutral and categorical/sequential/diverging scales. Use consistent semantic mappings and redundant labels/icons; color alone must not convey status. Aim for WCAG AA text contrast (4.5:1 normal, 3:1 large) and relevant non-text contrast. Example editorial palette: canvas #F5F3EE, surface #FFFFFF, text #202A28, muted #52615D, accent #285B4D, warning #946000, negative #A33C32. Alternative industrial dark: canvas #15201F, surface #22302E, text #F1F4F2, accent #9AC9B8. These are starting tokens, not audited palettes; test actual pairs. Do not assume cultural color meanings are universal.
## Typography
Choose a coherent sans or editorial serif/sans pairing, with CJK fallback and tabular numerals. Example desktop scale 12/14/16/22/32/48px, adjust for projection and density. Use line-height around 1.4–1.6 for prose, align numeric columns, show units, avoid tiny labels and all-caps Chinese headings. No unlicensed font redistribution.
## Layout
Select Matrix (monitoring/comparison), Editorial (claim/evidence), Hierarchical (overview/detail), Flow (sequence), Spatial (geographic/physical). Compose around one dominant task per scene. Use 4/8px spacing rhythm, aligned baselines, deliberate asymmetry, sufficient whitespace, direct chart annotations, adjacent evidence. Avoid equal cards by default; use tables for dense lookup. Responsive order must preserve meaning; test 390, 1440, 1920px widths.
## Material
Matte paper for editorial evidence; glass for contextual overlays with opaque fallback; parchment for historical/archive context; metal/instrument for industrial interfaces; terrain/solid volumes for spatial structure; wireframe for topology. Define role, opacity, texture, shadow and contrast per layer. Never obscure labels with blur, texture, specular effects or perspective. Material associations are design hypotheses, not universal psychology.

Ranking: sorted bar/dot; target deviation: diverging bar/bullet; time: line/small multiples; composition: stacked bar/treemap; distribution: histogram/box/ECDF; relationship: scatter; contribution: waterfall only for additive quantities; flow: Sankey only with reconciled flows; geography: choropleth for normalized rates, proportional symbols for totals; precise lookup: table. # Visual design execution rules
## Color
Define canvas, surface, text, muted, border, accent, positive, negative, warning, neutral and categorical/sequential/diverging scales. Use consistent semantic mappings and redundant labels/icons; color alone must not convey status. Aim for WCAG AA text contrast (4.5:1 normal, 3:1 large) and relevant non-text contrast. Example editorial palette: canvas #F5F3EE, surface #FFFFFF, text #202A28, muted #52615D, accent #285B4D, warning #946000, negative #A33C32. Alternative industrial dark: canvas #15201F, surface #22302E, text #F1F4F2, accent #9AC9B8. These are starting tokens, not audited palettes; test actual pairs. Do not assume cultural color meanings are universal.
## Typography
Choose a coherent sans or editorial serif/sans pairing, with CJK fallback and tabular numerals. Example desktop scale 12/14/16/22/32/48px, adjust for projection and density. Use line-height around 1.4–1.6 for prose, align numeric columns, show units, avoid tiny labels and all-caps Chinese headings. No unlicensed font redistribution.
## Layout
Select Matrix (monitoring/comparison), Editorial (claim/evidence), Hierarchical (overview/detail), Flow (sequence), Spatial (geographic/physical). Compose around one dominant task per scene. Use 4/8px spacing rhythm, aligned baselines, deliberate asymmetry, sufficient whitespace, direct chart annotations, adjacent evidence. Avoid equal cards by default; use tables for dense lookup. Responsive order must preserve meaning; test 390, 1440, 1920px widths.
## Material
Matte paper for editorial evidence; glass for contextual overlays with opaque fallback; parchment for historical/archive context; metal/instrument for industrial interfaces; terrain/solid volumes for spatial structure; wireframe for topology. Define role, opacity, texture, shadow and contrast per layer. Never obscure labels with blur, texture, specular effects or perspective. Material associations are design hypotheses, not universal psychology.
## Chart selection
Ranking: sorted bar/dot; target deviation: diverging bar/bullet; time: line/small multiples; composition: stacked bar/treemap; distribution: histogram/box/ECDF; relationship: scatter; contribution: waterfall only for additive quantities; flow: Sankey only with reconciled flows; geography: choropleth for normalized rates, proportional symbols for totals; precise lookup: table. Avoid 3D distortion of quantitative comparisons, misleading axes, fabricated uncertainty or causal claims.

# Visual design execution rules
## Color
Define canvas, surface, text, muted, border, accent, positive, negative, warning, neutral and categorical/sequential/diverging scales. Use consistent semantic mappings and redundant labels/icons; color alone must not convey status. Aim for WCAG AA text contrast (4.5:1 normal, 3:1 large) and relevant non-text contrast. Example editorial palette: canvas #F5F3EE, surface #FFFFFF, text #202A28, muted #52615D, accent #285B4D, warning #946000, negative #A33C32. Alternative industrial dark: canvas #15201F, surface #22302E, text #F1F4F2, accent #9AC9B8. These are starting tokens, not audited palettes; test actual pairs. Do not assume cultural color meanings are universal.
## Typography
Choose a coherent sans or editorial serif/sans pairing, with CJK fallback and tabular numerals. Example desktop scale 12/14/16/22/32/48px, adjust for projection and density. Use line-height around 1.4–1.6 for prose, align numeric columns, show units, avoid tiny labels and all-caps Chinese headings. No unlicensed font redistribution.
## Layout
Select Matrix (monitoring/comparison), Editorial (claim/evidence), Hierarchical (overview/detail), Flow (sequence), Spatial (geographic/physical). Compose around one dominant task per scene. Use 4/8px spacing rhythm, aligned baselines, deliberate asymmetry, sufficient whitespace, direct chart annotations, adjacent evidence. Avoid equal cards by default; use tables for dense lookup. Responsive order must preserve meaning; test 390, 1440, 1920px widths.
## Material
Matte paper for editorial evidence; glass for contextual overlays with opaque fallback; parchment for historical/archive context; metal/instrument for industrial interfaces; terrain/solid volumes for spatial structure; wireframe for topology. Define role, opacity, texture, shadow and contrast per layer. Never obscure labels with blur, texture, specular effects or perspective. Material associations are design hypotheses, not universal psychology.
## Chart selection
Ranking: sorted bar/dot; target deviation: diverging bar/bullet; time: line/small multiples; composition: stacked bar/treemap; distribution: histogram/box/ECDF; relationship: scatter; contribution: waterfall only for additive quantities; flow: Sankey only with reconciled flows; geography: choropleth for normalized rates, proportional symbols for totals; precise lookup: table. For engineering, architecture, science and networks consult domain routing and catalog. Separate canonical type from projection, material and animation. Avoid 3D distortion of quantitative comparisons, misleading axes, fabricated uncertainty or causal claims.
## Diagrams and space
Model nodes, edges, ports, groups and direction before layout. Use orthogonal routing or ELK when appropriate, minimize crossings without altering topology, preserve labels and swimlane semantics. Maps need grounded geometry, projection, legend and scale when relevant; simplified geometry must be labeled. 3D requires a genuine spatial task or clear illustrative purpose, not decorative extrusion alone. Never imply engineering-standard accuracy without verification.
## Motion and interaction
Define trigger, state, affected IDs, transition, duration, easing, interrupt/reset, keyboard/touch fallback. Suggested durations 120–250ms micro, 250–500ms scene, longer only for explanatory sequence; not mandatory. Maintain object constancy, preserve filters and selection, provide static/reduced-motion alternative. Use progressive disclosure, linked highlighting, drilldown, scenario presets, source inspection; essential evidence visible without hover. Model inputs must have bounds, units and assumptions. Avoid perpetual decorative animation.
## Visual specification
Record chosen art direction, rejected alternatives, token values, typography scale, layout per scene, chart encoding and rejected alternative, material roles, interaction state map, responsive strategy, and dependencies. # Semantic color

# Color art direction
Harmony is a compositional hypothesis, not a universal beauty law. Six hue relationships: monochrome, analogous, complementary, split complementary, triadic, neutral plus accent. Use neutral/support/accent area guide 75/20/5 only as starting heuristic, not measured pixel coverage. Visual weight depends on area, local contrast, saturation, position and surrounding content. Reserve high contrast for focal claims. Warm/cool meanings vary by culture and context. Preserve supplied brand hex exactly; restrict role if contrast fails, do not silently recolor. Keep semantic data palettes independent. Overlay helper approximates encoded sRGB source-over on one opaque backdrop; actual browser compositing, blur, gradients and layered materials need inspection. # Typography foundations V1.2
Typography is information hierarchy, not font decoration. Establish semantic roles before styling: display, heading, subheading, body, label, note, metric. Use size, weight, spacing, alignment and position before adding color. Do not force every role onto every page.
Three initial directions: editorial (serif headings, sans body), Swiss-inspired (sans hierarchy, grid), technical (compact sans, aligned numbers). These are candidate recipes, not historical reproductions. Font stacks are fallbacks, not bundled fonts; actual availability and CJK glyph coverage vary.
Numbers: use tabular lining figures for comparable columns if supported; align values by consistent units/precision, show minus signs and missing values explicitly; do not round away material differences. Large display metrics can use proportional figures. Decimal alignment needs layout support, not merely tabular figures.
Chinese/mixed: preserve punctuation and language-specific line breaking, avoid blanket letter spacing, avoid forced breaks inside Latin words and units where feasible; use lang attributes for language runs. 36em Chinese and 65ch English are starting measure heuristics, not accessibility requirements. CSS overflow-wrap anywhere is emergency wrapping. Test long labels, zoom, font fallback and narrow screens.

# Narrative Design V1.0
## Operating contract
Use for authored business narratives; for monitoring or exploratory dashboards, prioritize user tasks and do not manufacture a thesis. Never invent evidence, causal attribution, targets or user-test results. Distinguish observations, hypotheses, forecasts and decisions. Preserve contradictory evidence and source access.
## Workflow
1. G1 Evidence: inventory sources, grain, period, units, definitions, missingness and reconciliations. Stop on material unresolved errors; mark missing inputs.
2. G2 Thesis: generate three candidate questions or claims, compare relevance, support and actionability. Select one or retain an open question. Record rejected alternatives.
3. G3 Spine: choose a primary spine and archetype from references/atlas.md. Assign every chapter a role; remove redundant content without hiding material exceptions.
4. G4 Naked narrative: write a short executive summary and full prose argument. Link each material claim to evidence IDs; include counterevidence and uncertainty. Do not proceed if the argument fails.
5. G5 Storyboard: specify audience, time budget, cognitive before/after, chapter question, evidence, visual task, transition and interaction. Use templates/storyboard.json and schema. Essential information must be visible without interaction.
6. G6 Visual translation: choose encodings by task, not novelty; maintain units, scale, accessibility, stable object identity and responsive layout. Choose patterns from references/patterns.md only where justified.
7. G7 Implementation: use a shared data model for charts, tables and text. Test calculations, controls, keyboard navigation, reduced motion, narrow screens and missing data. Never present synthetic data as actual.
8. G8 Validation: run tests/protocol.md. Record actual results separately from predictions. No claim of superiority without comparative evidence.
## Required deliverables
Evidence map, thesis alternatives, naked narrative, storyboard JSON, implementation, validation log. For small tasks these may be concise sections rather than separate files. For executive reports default to conclusion first, then evidence, mechanism, options and explicit decision request; omit unsupported stages. For exploratory tools use a task-first path instead.
## Decision rules
Use a persistent scene only when object continuity matters. Use interaction only when it improves navigation, understanding, verification or decision-making. Provide a static fallback. Models must expose assumptions, valid ranges and limitations; do not infer behavioral effects from accounting identities. Preserve access to full evidence. A decision request must identify authority, options, constraints, owner and review trigger, or mark unknown.
